claim: Shared DELAY/WAIT countdown counter sized for WAIT's max reach (~1,015,808 cycles fits 20 bits) instead of DELAY's: DELAY exponent=3 with mantissa >= 32 silently truncates and ends ~1M cycles early.
spec_ref: docs/isa.md:Opcode table, DELAY row -- "cycles = mantissa << (exponent*5) ... exponent=3 -> up to ~16.7M (~335ms @ 50MHz)"

why_survives.directed: test_delay_timing uses only DELAY mantissa 0 and 6 at exponent 0.
why_survives.random: Default generator clamps DELAY to exponent 0/1 (mantissa <= 63 / <= 15). wide_timing (--full) emits exponent-3 DELAY only with mantissa 1 (32768 cycles, fits 20 bits) and exponent-2 with mantissa 1..4. WAIT's max timeout (31<<15) fits 20 bits, and wide WAITs resolve in a few cycles under the stimulus anyway.
why_survives.board: Protocol firmware uses exponent-0 DELAYs (<= ~250) and the I2C clock-stretch WAIT timeout 1<<15 = 32768, both fit 20 bits.
why_survives.formal: cycle_counter_timing_props catches early expiry only within BMC depth 20; truncated counts are always >= 32767 so expired never asserts early inside the window. core reset props 4b likewise only check DELAY occupancy within depth.
